title: DBMS Practice MCQs
subject: dbms
description: DBMS practice MCQs covering SQL, normalization, transactions, indexing, and keys for C-CAT exam preparation. Essential revision material for C-CAT aspirants.

questions.question: Can a Primary Key column contain a NULL value?
options: Yes, if it's a composite key
questions.explanation: A Primary Key must be unique and non-NULL by definition; it uniquely identifies each row.

questions.question: GRANT and REVOKE belong to which SQL command category?
questions.explanation: GRANT and REVOKE are DCL (Data Control Language) commands for managing permissions.

questions.question: What does 2NF specifically eliminate?
options: Partial dependency on a composite key
questions.explanation: 2NF eliminates partial dependencies — non-key attributes must depend on the entire composite key.

questions.question: What does 3NF specifically eliminate?
questions.explanation: 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies — non-key attributes must depend only on the primary key.

questions.question: Which join returns all rows from the left table, with NULLs where there's no match in the right?
How many clustered indexes can a single table have?
questions.explanation: A table can have only one clustered index because it determines the physical storage order of rows.

questions.question: In Two-Phase Locking, what happens once a transaction releases its first lock?
options: It can still acquire new locks freely
It cannot acquire any new locks — shrinking phase begins
The transaction is automatically rolled back
questions.explanation: In Two-Phase Locking, once a transaction releases its first lock, it enters the shrinking phase and cannot acquire new locks.
